purpose: Define config.rs's docgen.config.ts loading contract for the caliper-docgen CLI: the config path never enters the JavaScript source evaluated by the node+tsx subprocess as concatenated string content (making injection of arbitrary JS statements via a crafted path impossible), evaluation and validation failures are surfaced as hard errors rather than silently falling back to defaults, and CLI-flag-vs-config-file precedence is well-defined.
scope: crates/cli/src/config.rs and its call sites in extract.rs, watch.rs, check.rs, and inspect.rs (the four commands that call build_options). Covers: the node subprocess argument-passing mechanism, config-evaluation-failure and config-validation-failure error surfacing, and CLI-flag-over-config-file precedence rules. Does not cover the exit-code values these failures ultimately produce beyond what's asserted here (all four commands return exit code 1 on any config failure, consistent with SPEC-CLI-001a AC-010).
non_goals: The extraction/resolution logic itself — owned by crates/core, a separate capability under a separate spec.
NAPI/Node binding entry points — owned by crates/binding, a separate capability.
schema, lsp, and completions' handling of --config beyond AC-008 (they accept it syntactically but never read it) — their exit codes and other behavior are covered by SPEC-CLI-001a/001c.

Validating docgen.config.ts fields beyond the two examples (reactVersion, unsupported field name) exercised here — a full config-schema validation matrix is separate work if more fields need dedicated criteria.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given a --config path or discovered docgen.config.ts path whose directory or file name contains, in any combination, a single quote ('), a double quote ("), a backslash (\), a newline, or the literal sequence "');process.exit(1);('", config loading still evaluates the target file's actual JavaScript/TypeScript content and produces the same PipelineOptions as an equivalent path without those characters, and no additional JavaScript statement from the path's content is ever executed — specifically, the process does not exit early with code 1 from the exit(1) sequence above, and no file, process, or other side effect results from those characters being interpreted as JavaScript syntax rather than literal path text. (Implementation note, not part of the pass/fail check: this is achieved by passing the path via the __DOCGEN_CONFIG_PATH environment variable rather than concatenating it into the script string handed to node's stdin — a string-concatenation implementation such as `format!("const p = '{}'; ...", path)` would fail this criterion for the quote and exit(1) cases above even though it defeats simple shell-metacharacter payloads.)

When docgen.config.ts exists but fails to evaluate (e.g. a JavaScript/TypeScript syntax error), extract, watch, check, and inspect (the only four commands that call build_options) each return exit code 1 with an error message that includes the real underlying node/tsx error output (e.g. text containing 'SyntaxError' or an esbuild 'Expected identifier' message), and none of the four falls back to default PipelineOptions.

When --config PATH names a file that does not exist but whose parent directory does exist, extract, watch, check, and inspect each return exit code 1, surfacing node's own dynamic-import failure (including node's stderr output) as a hard error rather than silently falling back to defaults or to ancestor-walk discovery.

When --config PATH's parent directory does not exist, extract, watch, check, and inspect each return exit code 1, surfaced from the node subprocess's own Command::spawn failure (which fails because current_dir is set to a nonexistent directory) rather than a node dynamic-import error, and none of the four falls back to defaults or to ancestor-walk discovery. (Current behavior note: the surfaced message is the static 'Failed to spawn node to evaluate docgen.config.ts — is node installed and on PATH?' wrap plus the OS's 'No such file or directory' error — it does not include PATH itself, since std::io::Error from a bad current_dir carries no path. Compare AC-003, whose node-dynamic-import error does include the path via node's own ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND message.)

When docgen.config.ts's default export contains a field name not in the supported config schema (including a typo of a supported field name), extract, watch, check, and inspect each return exit code 1 with an error message containing the unrecognized field name exactly as it appeared in the config file's default export, rather than silently ignoring the field.

When docgen.config.ts sets reactVersion to a string other than "react18" or "react19", extract, watch, check, and inspect each return exit code 1 with an error message containing the bad value, rather than silently defaulting to react19.

For extract, watch, check, and inspect: a --config PATH flag takes precedence over docgen.config.ts auto-discovery by walking up from the current working directory, and for all four, a non-empty --src list overrides srcDirs from a loaded config file (the only config-overridable flag WatchArgs, CheckArgs, and InspectArgs expose). extract's ExtractArgs additionally exposes --no-cross-package, --react-version, --cache-dir, --html-attributes, and --extra-builtins; when passed, each of these overrides its corresponding config field (crossPackage, reactVersion, cacheDir, htmlAttributes, extraBuiltins respectively) — but watch, check, and inspect have no such flags, so for those three, crossPackage/reactVersion/cacheDir/htmlAttributes/extraBuiltins are always taken from the loaded config file (or its defaults) as-is, with no CLI override possible.

schema, lsp, and completions accept the global --config flag at argument-parsing time (it is defined once on Cli, not per-subcommand) but none of cmd_schema, cmd_lsp, or cmd_completions calls build_options/try_load_config — passing --config to any of these three has no observable effect on their output or exit code.
